questions.question: The ratio of the speed of a bus to that of a train is 15 ∶ 27. Also, a car covers a distance of 720 km in 9 hours. The speed of the bus is three-fourths of the speed of the car. How much distance will the train cover in 7 hours?
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of the speed of a bus to that of a train is 15 ∶ 27. 

Also, a car covers a distance of 720 km in 9 hours. 

The speed of the bus is three-fourths of the speed of the car. 

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Speed of the car = 720/9 = 80 km/h

So, speed of the bus = 3/4 × 80 = 60 km/h

So, speed of the train = 27 × (60 ÷ 15) = 108 km/h

Now, the distance that the train will cover in 7 hours = 108 × 7 = 756 km

∴ The train will cover 756 km.

questions.solution:
Given:

Walking at (3)/(4) of this usual speed, a man covers a certain distance in 1 hour and 40 minutes more than the time he takes to cover the distance at his usual speed. 

Concept used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

1 hour 40 minutes = (1 + 40/60) hours

⇒ (1 + 2/3) = 5/3 hours

Let the usual speed and distance be Q km/h and D km respectively.

Time taken to cover the distance in usual speed = D/Q hours

According to the question,

D/(3Q/4) - D/Q = 5/3

⇒ 4D/3Q - D/Q = 5/3

⇒ D/Q × 1/3 = 5/3

⇒ D/Q = 5

**∴ The time taken by him to cover the same distance at his usual speed is 5 hours.**

questions.solution:

The time taken by R to cover 45 km is 1.2 hours.

Distance to be covered = 400 meters

Speed = Distance / Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed = 45,000 / 4320 meters/second

⇒ Speed = 10.42 meters/second

Time = 400 meters / 10.42 meters/second

⇒ Time = 38.4 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A car covers the first 140 km of a journey in 10 hours and the next 260 km in 15 hours. What is the average speed of the Car for the whole journey?
questions.solution:

The first 140 km of a journey in 10 hours and the next 260 km in 15 hours.

**Formula used**

Average speed = Total distance/Total time

**Calculation**

Total time = 10 + 15 = 25 hours

Average speed = 400/25 = 16 km/hr.

**The answer is 16 km/hr**

questions.question: Piu and Titu start from the same place at the same time and walk in opposite directions. If Piu walks at 5 km/h and Titu walks at 2 km/h, after what time will they be 10.5 km apart?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When moving in opposite directions, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 5 + 2 = 7 km/h

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 10.5 ÷ 7 = 1.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Piu = 5 km/h

Speed of Titu = 2 km/h

Total distance apart = 10.5 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (in opposite directions) = Speed₁ + Speed₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba8796fe745a1a0db7716794a5218920445b309df5e4ed51bc66876cad29776b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time taken for them to be 10.5 km apart be t hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Piu in time t = 5 × t = 5t km

⇒ Distance covered by Titu in time t = 2 × t = 2t km

⇒ Since they are moving in opposite directions, the total distance is the sum of their individual distances.

⇒ Total distance = 5t + 2t

⇒ 7t = 10.5

⇒ t = 10.5 ÷ 7

⇒ t = 1.5 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds. Relative Speed = |Speed₁ − Speed₂|.

Average Speed

If an object covers two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂ respectively, the overall average speed is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: The speed of a car is 1(1)/(5) times the speed of a bus. A train covers 1200 km in 15 hours. How much distance will the car cover in 7 hours if the speed of the bus is 1(1)/(4) times the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed of **Train** = 1200 ÷ 15 = 80 kmph.

Speed of **Bus** = 80 × (5/4) = 100 kmph.

Speed of **Car** = 100 × (6/5) = 120 kmph.

**Distance** covered by Car = 120 × 7 = 840 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 840 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of **Train** = 1200 km, Time = 15 hours.

Speed of **Bus** = 1(1/4) × Speed of Train = 5/4 × Speed of Train.

Speed of **Car** = 1(1/5) × Speed of Bus = 6/5 × Speed of Bus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/88df3d5e327438cd4e3324dd4da86c101ab282c370de1b40664216181882e15b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of **Train** = Distance ÷ Time = 1200 ÷ 15 = 80 kmph.

⇒ Speed of **Bus** = 80 × (5/4) = 100 kmph.

⇒ Speed of **Car** = 100 × (6/5) = 120 kmph.

⇒ Distance covered by **Car** = Speed of Car × Time = 120 × 7

⇒ Distance = 840 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 840 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance Formula

Basic relationship: Distance = Speed × Time. To find speed, use Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: If Ramesh walks at a speed of 15 km/h, instead of 12 km/h, he would have walked 2 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance (in km) travelled by Ramesh at 12 km/h in the same time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramesh's normal speed = 12 km/h

Ramesh's increased speed = 15 km/h

Distance increased due to increased speed = 2 km

**Concept used: **

The concept of speed, time, and distance.

**Solution:**

Let's denote the time Ramesh spent walking as 't'.

Distance covered at normal speed = Speed × Time = 12t

Distance covered at increased speed = Speed × Time = 15t

According to the question, 15t = 12t + 2

Solving for 't', we get t = 2 / 3 hours

Substituting 't' back into the distance equation, Distance = 12t = 12 × 2/3 = 8 km

**Therefore, the actual distance travelled by Ramesh at 12 km/h in the same time is 8 km.**

questions.question: Zakir travels from City A to City B. If Zakir drives his car at (2)/(3) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 10 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Zakir would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Speed Ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 2

Time Ratio (Normal : New) = 2 : 3

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

1 unit = 10 minutes, therefore normal time (2 units) = 20 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = 2/3 × Normal speed

Time difference = 10 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the distance between City A and City B is constant:

⇒ Normal Speed × Normal Time = New Speed × New Time

⇒ S × T = (2S / 3) × (T + 10)

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance travelled is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional. This implies that if speed is multiplied by a fraction a/b, the time taken will be multiplied by its reciprocal b/a.

Distance Formula

Distance = Speed × Time. It connects the three foundational elements of kinematics. Ensuring consistent units (e.g., kmph for speed and hours for time) is critical for accurate calculations.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If equal distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: If a boy goes from his home to his school at a speed of 40 km/h, he reaches 10 minutes early. If he goes at a speed of 35 km/h, he reaches 5 minutes late. What will be the time taken for the journey at a speed of 35 km/h?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio of speeds** is S₁ : S₂ = 40 : 35 = 8 : 7.

Since the **distance** between home and school is **constant**, the **time ratio** is the inverse of the speed ratio: T₁ : T₂ = 7 : 8.

The **total difference in time** between being early and late is 10 + 5 = 15 min.

In the ratio, the difference (8 − 7) = 1 unit → 15 min.

Therefore, the **time taken at 35 km/h** (which corresponds to 8 units) = 8 × 15 = 120 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Initial speed** (S₁) = 40 km/h (reaches 10 min early)

**Reduced speed** (S₂) = 35 km/h (reaches 5 min late)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2b3c1820f0d9979068a3b8a80b67d32d992c1f77330d8dfac445b5d0953eee3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ − S₂) ] × ΔT

Where ΔT is the **total time difference** in hours.

**Calculations:**

⇒ ΔT = (10 + 5) min = 15 min = 15/60 hours = 1/4 hours

⇒ D = [ (40 × 35) ÷ (40 − 35) ] × (1/4)

⇒ D = [ 1400 ÷ 5 ] × (1/4)

⇒ D = 280 × (1/4) = 70 km

⇒ **Time taken** at speed 35 km/h = Distance ÷ S₂

⇒ Time = 70 ÷ 35 = 2 hours

⇒ 2 hours = 2 × 60 = 120 min

**∴ The correct answer is 120 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Distance, Speed, and Time Relationship

The fundamental relation is **Distance = Speed × Time**. When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T).

Average Speed Formula

If a person travels equal distances at speeds x and y, the **average speed** for the whole journey is given by (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

Time taken by fast train to cover 192 km = 192/(x + 16) hrs

questions.question: Points A and B are 200 km apart. A person starts from A at 10 a.m. at a speed of 10 km/h and goes towards B. Another person starts from B at 11 a.m.at a speed of 20 km/h and goes towards A. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Distance covered** by the first person in 1 hour (10 a.m. to 11 a.m.) = 10 × 1 = 10 km.

**Remaining distance** to be covered at 11 a.m. = 200 − 10 = 190 km.

**Relative speed** (moving towards each other) = 10 + 20 = 30 km/h.

**Time taken** to meet after 11 a.m. = 190 ÷ 30 = 6 hours 20 minutes.

Meeting time = 11:00 a.m. + 6 hours 20 minutes = 5:20 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5:20 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 200 km

Speed of person from A (S₁) = 10 km/h (Starts at 10 a.m.)

Speed of person from B (S₂) = 20 km/h (Starts at 11 a.m.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/22b20619ad287320cd050d27fb3de0f47a5a37f964727bde2cc3bb7c4b7d9bd1.png] 

Step 1: Calculate the distance covered by the first person before the second person starts.

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour = 10 km/h × 1 h = 10 km.

Step 2: Find the remaining distance between them at 11 a.m.

⇒ Remaining Distance = 200 − 10 = 190 km.

Step 3: Calculate the relative speed as they are moving towards each other.

⇒ Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂ = 10 + 20 = 30 km/h.

Step 4: Calculate the time required to cover the remaining distance.

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 190 ÷ 30 = 19/3 hours

⇒ Time = 6 hours + (1/3) × 60 minutes = 6 hours 20 minutes.

Step 5: Determine the final meeting time.

⇒ Meeting Time = 11:00 a.m. + 6 hours 20 minutes = 5:20 p.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5:20 p.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the **sum of their individual speeds** (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the same direction, it is the **difference** (|S₁ − S₂|).

Synchronization of Time

Before applying the relative speed formula, always ensure both objects are calculated from the **same starting time** by finding the distance one has already covered.

Time, Speed, and Distance Formula

The fundamental relation is **Distance = Speed × Time**. Ensure units are consistent (e.g., km and km/h or m and m/s).</p

questions.question: Ramesh and Naresh start running at speeds of 26 km/h and 18 km/h respectively towards each other, they meet after one hour and 45 minutes. How far (in metres) were they from each other when they started running?
questions.solution:
**Given data:**

Speed of Ramesh = 26 km/h, Speed of Naresh = 18 km/h, time = 1 hour 45 minutes = 1.75 hours

**Concept:**

Distance covered is the product of speed and time.

**Solution:**

Total distance covered = (Speed of Ramesh + Speed of Naresh) × Time

⇒ (26 km/h + 18 km/h) × 1.75 hours = 77 km = 77,000 m

**Therefore, they were 77,000 m apart when they started running.**

questions.question: A girl goes from A to B with speed 60 km/hr and return from B to A with speed 30 km/hr. If whole journey takes 5 hours, then what is the distance between A and B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a person travels a certain distance at speed S₁ and returns at speed S₂ taking total time T, the distance is given by:

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂) ] × Total Time

Distance = [ (60 × 30) ÷ (60 + 30) ] × 5

Distance = [ 1800 ÷ 90 ] × 5 = 20 × 5 = 100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 60 km/hr

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 30 km/hr

Total time taken (T) = 5 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db13c818c5460bd7700857e1bfe0a86e1e29c2019966f1744c3f965a2e2612bd.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

Let the total distance between A and B be D km.

⇒ Time taken to travel from A to B = D ÷ 60 hours

⇒ Time taken to return from B to A = D ÷ 30 hours

The total time for the whole journey is given as 5 hours.

⇒ (D ÷ 60) + (D ÷ 30) = 5

⇒ (D + 2D) ÷ 60 = 5

⇒ 3D ÷ 60 = 5

⇒ D ÷ 20 = 5

⇒ D = 20 × 5

⇒ D = 100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When an object covers two equal distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the entire journey is calculated as (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Average Speed (Equal Time Intervals)

When an object travels at speed S₁ for a certain time and at speed S₂ for an equal amount of time, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed

If two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). If they are moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).
</p

questions.question: The speeds of three cars are in the ratio 5 : 3 : 4. The ratio between the time taken by these cars to cover the same distance is.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The speeds of three cars are in the ratio 5:3:4.

**Formula Used:**

Time taken = Distance / Speed

Ratio of time taken = Inverse ratio of speeds

**Calculation:**

Speeds of cars are in the ratio 5:3:4

Let the speeds be 5x, 3x, and 4x respectively.

To cover the same distance, time taken is inversely proportional to speed.

Therefore, ratio of time taken = 1/(5x) : 1/(3x) : 1/(4x)

⇒ Ratio of time taken = 1/5 : 1/3 : 1/4

⇒ Ratio of time taken = 12 : 20 : 15

**The ratio between the time taken by these cars to cover the same distance is 12 : 20 : 15.**

questions.question: A man takes 30 minutes to cover a certain distance at the speed of 8 km/h, If he walks at a speed of 16 km/h, he covers the same distance in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **speed** and **time** are inversely proportional (Speed ∝ 1/Time).

Ratio of **speeds** (S₁ : S₂) = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2.

Ratio of **times** (T₁ : T₂) = 2 : 1.

Given 2 units = 30 min, then 1 unit = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Speed** (S₁) = 8 km/h

Initial **Time** (T₁) = 30 min = 0.5 hours

New **Speed** (S₂) = 16 km/h

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b3110cadefbf40b9e0dd53ae35b7312c41558e6d50016c99333b24bc7574b97.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Distance** = 8 × (30 ÷ 60) km

⇒ **Distance** = 8 × 0.5 = 4 km

⇒ New **Time** (T₂) = **Distance** ÷ New **Speed**

⇒ T₂ = 4 ÷ 16 = 0.25 hours

⇒ T₂ in minutes = 0.25 × 60 = 15 min

**∴ The correct answer is 15 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

If **distance** is constant, then S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂. This allows for direct calculation of the unknown variable without finding the distance first.

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **minutes** to **hours**, divide by 60.

Average Speed

When two equal distances are covered at speeds **x** and **y**, the **average speed** is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: If a train runs at 6/7th of its original speed, then it reaches the station 20 minutes late. Find out the usual time taken by train to cover the distance.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Speed** (Original : New) = 7 : 6.

Since **Distance** is constant, Ratio of **Time** (Original : New) = 6 : 7.

Difference in **Time** units = 7 − 6 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 20 min.

Usual **Time** = 6 units = 6 × 20 = 120 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New **Speed** = 6/7 of Original **Speed**.

Time delay = 20 **min**.

**Formula Used:**

**Distance** = **Speed** × **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acd7f511e53fae5317743a0b310bc1f5087d35da1c81dfdb1fb442f3f5304007.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **usual speed** be S and **usual time** be T.

⇒ New **Speed** (S′) = 6S/7

⇒ New **Time** (T′) = T + 20

⇒ Since **Distance** is constant, S × T = S′ × T′

⇒ S × T = (6S/7) × (T + 20)

⇒ T = (6/7) × (T + 20)

⇒ 7T = 6T + 120

⇒ T = 120 **min**

**∴ The correct answer is 120 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation

When the **distance** is constant, the **speed** is inversely proportional to the **time** taken (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a.

Average Speed Formula

If a certain **distance** is covered at speed x and the same distance is covered at speed y, the **average speed** for the whole journey is 2xy / (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, their **relative speed** is the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).</p

questions.question: A man completes a journey in 12 h. He travels the first half of the journey at a speed of 21 km/h and the second half at a speed of 24 km/h. Find the total distance of the journey (in km).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed for two equal halves of a journey = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average speed = (2 × 21 × 24) ÷ (21 + 24) = 1008 ÷ 45 = 22.4 km/h

Total Distance = Average Speed × Total Time

Total Distance = 22.4 × 12 = 268.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 268.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for first half (S₁) = 21 km/h

Speed for second half (S₂) = 24 km/h

Total time (T) = 12 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edacaefe90deff5bceebe8f793d2412702537f6945bada6f16a8334776343fde.png] 

Let the total distance be D km.

⇒ Time for first half = (D ÷ 2) ÷ 21 = D ÷ 42 hours

⇒ Time for second half = (D ÷ 2) ÷ 24 = D ÷ 48 hours

⇒ Total Time = D ÷ 42 + D ÷ 48 = 12

⇒ (8D + 7D) ÷ 336 = 12 [LCM of 42 and 48 is 336]

⇒ 15D ÷ 336 = 12

⇒ 15D = 12 × 336

⇒ 15D = 4032

⇒ D = 4032 ÷ 15

⇒ D = 268.8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 268.8 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

It is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Conversion of Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Proportionality Rule

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If time is constant, distance is directly proportional to speed (D ∝ S).</p

questions.question: A person travels one-third of a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h, and the remaining distance at a speed of 60 km/h. If he travels this distance at a uniform speed taking the same time, then what will be his speed (in km/h)?

questions.question: Abhishek climbs up a hill at a speed of 3 mi/h and comes down at a speed of 5 mi/h. If the total time taken for the two-way journey is 10 hours, then what is the distance between the hilltop and the foothill?

Shreya hikes up a hill at 3 mi/h and comes down at 5 mi/h. The total time taken for the two-way journey is 10 hours.

questions.question: A dog takes 5 leaps for every 6 leaps of a hare, but 4 leaps of the dog are equal to 5 leaps of the hare. The ratio of the speed of dog and hare is?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Write the **number of leaps** for both animals in the first row and their **leap equivalence** in the second row.

**Dog** : 5 leaps | **Hare** : 6 leaps

Equivalence: 4 Dog leaps = 5 Hare leaps

To find the **Speed Ratio**, cross-multiply the number of leaps with the opposite animal's equivalence factor.

Speed Ratio = (5 × 5) : (6 × 4) = 25 : 24

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of leaps: **Dog** = 5, **Hare** = 6

Leap distance ratio: 4 **Dog leaps** = 5 **Hare leaps**

**Formula Used:**

**Speed** = (Number of leaps in given time) × (Distance covered in each leap)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8f3d426b0e51aff3b1af7fcfdba9f2b8838ad59f5bc612436dafa9349048cfb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance of 1 **Dog leap** be D and 1 **Hare leap** be H.

⇒ According to the question: 4 × D = 5 × H

⇒ D / H = 5 / 4

⇒ Speed of **Dog** (Sd) = 5 × D

⇒ Speed of **Hare** (Sₕ) = 6 × H

⇒ Ratio = (Sd) / (Sₕ) = (5 × D) / (6 × H)

⇒ Ratio = (5 / 6) × (D / H)

⇒ Substituting the value of D/H: Ratio = (5 / 6) × (5 / 4)

⇒ Ratio = 25 / 24

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Distance Relationship

When time is constant, **Speed** is directly proportional to the **Distance** covered. In leap problems, distance depends on both frequency and leap length.

Leap Length Units

If x leaps of A = y leaps of B, then the ratio of their leap lengths is **Length A : Length B = y : x**.

Ratio Multiplication

To find the resultant ratio of speed, always multiply the **Frequency Ratio** by the **Distance Ratio** of each individual step.</p

questions.question: Ramesh walks a certain distance and rides back in 5 hours 45 minutes. If he could ride both ways in 3 hours 30 minutes, find the time required by Ramesh to walk both ways
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Ramesh to walk a certain distance and ride back = 5 hours 45 minutes

Time taken to ride both ways = 3 hours 30 minutes

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time taken to walk both ways = 3 hours 30 minutes

⇒ We know that, 1 hour = 60 minutes

⇒ So, time taken to walk both ways = 180 + 30 = 210 minutes

⇒ Time taken to walk only a single way = 210 ÷ 2 = 105 minutes

⇒ Time taken to walk one way and ride back = 5 hours 45 minutes = 345 minutes

⇒ Time taken to walk only a single way = 345 – 105 = 240 minutes

⇒ Then, time taken to walk both the ways = 240 × 2 = 480 minutes

⇒ 480 minutes = 480 ÷ 60 = 8 hours

**Therefore, the time required by Ramesh to walk both the ways is 8 hours.**

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Difference in Speed = 95 − 80 = 15 km/h.

Total Speed = 95 + 80 = 175 km/h.

Total Distance = (Total Speed ÷ Difference in Speed) × Difference in Distance

Total Distance = (175 ÷ 15) × 180 = 175 × 12 = 2100 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of first train = 80 km/h

Speed of second train = 95 km/h

Difference in distance travelled at meeting time = 180 km

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3936af0792450c651f57e7a2494dda9a5685edd766a57df7ceb79b4c9b013cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the time taken for both trains to meet be t hours.

⇒ Distance covered by first train = 80 × t

⇒ Distance covered by second train = 95 × t

⇒ The difference in distance covered = 95t − 80t = 15t

⇒ 15t = 180

⇒ t = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 hours

⇒ Total distance between Bangalore and Chennai = 80t + 95t = 175t

⇒ Total distance = 175 × 12

⇒ Total distance = 2100 km

**∴ The correct answer is 2100 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Constant Time Property

If two objects travel for the exact same amount of time, the ratio of distances they cover is equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ ÷ D₂ = S₁ ÷ S₂).
</p

questions.question: Manav starts from a place A and reaches the place B in 29 hours. He travels 2/9 distance at the speed of 9 km/hr and the remaining distance at the speed of 12 km/hr. What is the distance between A and B?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total time taken = 29 hours

Distance covered at speed 1 = 2/9 of the total distance

Speed 1 = 9 km/hr

Speed 2 = 12 km/hr

**Let the total distance be:**

D km

**Calculations:**

Distance covered at speed 1 = (2/9)D

Distance covered at speed 2 = (7/9)D

**Time taken for the first part:**

Time = Distance / Speed = (2/9)D / 9 = (2D / 81) hours

**Time taken for the second part:**

Time = (7/9)D / 12 = (7D / 108) hours

**Total time:**

⇒ Total time = Time for first part + Time for second part

⇒ 29 = (2D / 81) + (7D / 108)

**Finding a common denominator (for 81 and 108):**

⇒ LCM(81, 108) = 324

⇒ 29 = (8D / 324) + (21D / 324)

⇒ 29 = (29D / 324)

⇒ 29 × 324 = 29D

⇒ D = 324 km

**∴ The distance between A and B is 324 km.**

questions.question: P and Q start from the same point and at the same time with speeds 20 km/hr and 16 km/hr respectively. What is the distance between P and Q after 4 hours if both move in same direction?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in the **same direction**, their **Relative Speed** is the difference between their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 20 km/hr − 16 km/hr = 4 km/hr.

**Distance** = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 4 km/hr × 4 hr = 16 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **P** (SP) = 20 km/hr

Speed of **Q** (SQ) = 16 km/hr

**Time** (T) = 4 hr

⇒ Distance covered by **P** in 4 hr = 20 × 4 = 80 km.

⇒ Distance covered by **Q** in 4 hr = 16 × 4 = 64 km.

⇒ Required **Distance between P and Q** = Distance of P − Distance of Q

⇒ Distance = 80 km − 64 km = 16 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds u and v ( v), the relative speed is (u − v).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions at speeds u and v, the relative speed is (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance Constant Rule

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T).</p

questions.question: An athlete crosses a 3000-m distance in 10 minutes. What is his speed (in km/h)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 3000 m = 3 km, Time = 10 minutes = 10/60 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Speed = 3 km / (10/60) hours

⇒ Speed = 3 km / (1/6) hours

⇒ Speed = 3 × 6 km/h

⇒ Speed = 18 km/h

**The speed of the athlete is 18 km/h.**

questions.question: The speed of a car is 90 km/h. The distance covered by the car in 7 Seconds will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the car = 90 km/h.

Time = 7 Seconds.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Note: The speed should be in km/s or m/s and the time in seconds to find the distance in meters.

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculation:**

First, convert speed from km/h to m/s:

Speed in m/s = 90 × 5/18

Speed in m/s = 25 m/s

Now, calculate the distance:

Distance = Speed × Time

Distance = 25 × 7

Distance = 175 metres

**The distance covered by the car in 7 seconds is 175 metres.**
